Title: Fatal Gua Musang crash survivor makes positive progress
Article:
GUA MUSANG: A 21-year-old woman who was critically injured in a crash that claimed three lives along the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai Road near Gua Sejuk yesterday is showing positive progress after being transferred to Sultan Ismail Petra Hospital (HSIP), Kuala Krai, for further treatment.
The victim, Nur Balqis Abli, is currently being treated in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) and remains sedated, according to her uncle Mohamad Emerul Hakim Abdullah.
He said the eldest of four siblings suffered critical injuries, including bleeding in the head, liver and lungs, following the accident.
"After several CT scans were conducted, doctors found that her condition was improving," he told reporters when contacted today.
In the incident at about 7am yesterday, Nur Balqis' mother and younger brother were among three people killed when the Perodua Myvi they were travelling in from Kuala Krai towards Gua Musang lost control, entered the opposite lane and collided with a trailer.
Another victim killed was the Perodua Myvi driver, Muhamad Syazwan Hakimi Ibrahim, 21, while the trailer driver escaped unhurt.
The remains of Nur Balqis' mother and younger brother were buried at the Kampung Melor Lama Muslim Cemetery, Kota Bharu, while Muhamad Syazwan Hakimi's remains were laid to rest at the Kampung Tegayong Muslim Cemetery, Melor, Kota Baru, this morning.

Title: NS polls: EC pilots digital voter attendance system at polling centre
Article:
SEREMBAN: The diverse demographic profile of voters at Sekolah Menengah Agama (SMA) Dato Klana Petra Maamor near Ampangan made it the ideal location for the Election Commission's (EC) pilot Optical Character Recognition Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system during the Negri Sembilan election.
The OCR-VA system was developed to record and verify voter attendance at polling streams by automatically scanning information on voters' identity cards.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the commission was using seven polling streams at the school for the pilot project, marking the first step towards digitalising voter attendance records.
"We want to observe different voter profiles, including senior citizens, young voters and others.
"We believe this school is suitable in terms of its size and voter composition to serve as the pilot project," he said at a press conference after observing the voting process at SMA Dato Klana Petra Maamor in Ampangan today.
Ramlan said the project was intended to determine whether identity cards could be used to record voter attendance instead of the current manual process.
"This system does not involve any aspect of the electoral process. It is merely a pilot project that we believe is a positive step forward.
"Through the OCR-VA system, we can obtain real-time information on voter turnout, including gender and age group," he said.
He said the system had yet to be officially implemented as the commission wanted to evaluate the findings of the pilot project first.
"Based on today's findings, we will obtain more detailed information.
"After that, we will seek feedback from all stakeholders. We will not implement the system without first consulting the relevant parties," he said.
Earlier, the media reported that the EC would conduct the OCR-VA pilot project during today's 16th Negri Sembilan election.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus was reported as saying the system was introduced as part of efforts to improve the management of the electoral process.

Title: Sabah to secure 40pc stake in floating LNG project, says Hajiji
Article:
KALABAKAN: Sabah is set to sign an agreement with Petronas that will see the state acquire a 40 per cent stake in a floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) project.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the milestone was made possible through a cooperation agreement previously signed with Petronas, enabling the state government to participate more actively in Sabah's oil and gas industry.
"We have successfully reached an agreement with Petronas, and in the next few months, we will sign an agreement under which Sabah will receive a 40 per cent stake in the state's floating LNG project.
"In Sandakan, Petronas has secured an oil and gas field, and Sabah will receive a 20 per cent stake in the project there," he said after officiating the Kalabakan parliamentary constituency Jelajah Rakyat Programme and Madani Rahmah Sales Programme at the Kalabakan District Office Open Hall here.
Hajiji said the state and its people stood to benefit significantly from the strong relationship between the state and federal governments.
He said Sabah continued to attract growing investor interest due to the state government's investor-friendly policies, a fact acknowledged by foreign diplomats who had visited the state to explore investment opportunities.
"Nearly 40 foreign diplomats or high commissioners have met me over the past five years.
"They are attracted to our investor-friendly policies. They believe these policies will propel Sabah towards a brighter future, and that is exactly what we are working to achieve," he said.
Hajiji said existing industrial areas, particularly the Kota Kinabalu Industrial Park (KKIP) and the Sipitang Oil and Gas Industrial Park (SOGIP), were approaching full capacity due to strong investor demand.
As a result, he said, the state government was expanding new industrial zones, including the Palm Oil Industrial Cluster (POIC) on the east coast and industrial parks based on the blue economy.

Title: 20,000 Cambodians still unable to return home after Thai clashes: UN
Article:
BANGKOK: More than 20,000 Cambodians remain displaced along the border with Thailand following last year's clashes, a UN expert said Friday, urging both sides to resolve the crisis.
A long-standing border dispute erupted into fighting in July and December, killing dozens of people. Thailand and Cambodia agreed to a ceasefire deal in December, but they have repeatedly accused each other of truce violations.
"International law is very clear that those who have been displaced in a situation like this in a conflict have the right to go home," Tom Andrews, the newly appointed UN special rapporteur on human rights in Cambodia, told AFP in an interview.
In a statement after his visit to the border, Andrews said 650,000 Cambodian civilians were displaced by the end of 2025 and 20,000 still were.
Some towns and villages were now occupied by Thai soldiers, he said, while barbed wire and barriers blocked people from returning home.
"I saw houses with bullet holes.. a bomb in the midst of the rubble," he told AFP, adding: "This crisis has to be addressed as quickly as possible because of the human suffering involved."
Bangkok insists it has merely reclaimed Thai land that Cambodians had been occupying.
- STILL SCAMMING -
Andrews concluded his first official visit to Cambodia on Friday, where he also raised concerns about the victims trafficked to work in scam centres, and wider restrictions on political rights.
Cambodia has emerged as a hub for crime syndicates running fake romantic relationship and cryptocurrency investment schemes in which scammers defraud internet users around the world.
Andrews said more than 600 scam centres were raided and thousands of people had been arrested, but "the scamming continues", spreading from towns and cities into rural areas, based in individual homes and even cars.
The fate of those who were trafficked to work in the scam centres remains unclear, he said in a telephone interview.
He said he had heard reports of thousands of people living on the streets without money or passports, but said the authorities assured him there was a "process of vetting" underway to differentiate victims from criminals, even if it faced a "capacity issue."
Andrews said he also pressed Cambodia's leaders to ensure everyone implicated in the scam centres faced justice, including high-level officials.
"I emphasised the importance of accountability for all, not just those on the bottom rung of the ladder, but those at the top," he said.
- POLITICAL RIGHTS -
Andrews said there had been in general "frank discussions" about the rights situation in Cambodia, led for more than 40 years by former leader Hun Sen and his son, Prime Minister Hun Manet.
"The examples that I've been provided of the denial of rights, political intimidation – overt and subtle – need to be addressed," he said.
Among the people he met with was Kem Sokha, the leader of Cambodia's banned opposition party.
Recently pardoned after serving nearly a decade of a 27-year sentence for treason, Kem Sokha's political rights, including holding office and voting, remain revoked.
He said he told both Hun Sen and Hun Manet that "there are two forms of detention – there's the detention of the person and there's the detention of their rights."
"Kem Sokha the person has been released but his political rights have not."
He said he would be closely following how key rights such as freedom of expression and association were observed as Cambodia gears up for local elections next year and a general election due in 2028.
In a message to rights activists, he concluded: "Even though they may feel isolated, they're not. People are paying attention."--AFP

Title: Tengku Permaisuri Selangor outraged over animal cruelty
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Hajah Norashikin, has expressed her profound sorrow, disappointment and anger over recurring acts of cruelty towards domestic pets and stray animals, particularly dogs and cats that continue to go viral.
As the Royal Patron of the Stray Free Selangor (SFS) initiative under SPCA Selangor, Her Royal Highness said torturing, injuring, killing, or mistreating animals not only violates the law, but also reflects a failure to uphold basic human compassion and the fundamental values of a civilised society.
In a statement posted on Facebook, she said no form of animal cruelty will be accepted or tolerated under any circumstances, regardless of the perpetrator's background, designation, race or religion. (SLUG: HRH)
"This unyielding stance applies universally across all individuals, organisations, corporations, government agencies, and authorities, asserting that no one is above the law," she said.
Her Royal Highness added that any party found committing acts of animal abuse must be investigated and subjected to appropriate legal action, even if the offenses involve enforcement officers themselves.
"Public trust in enforcement agencies can only be preserved when actions are carried out professionally, with integrity, and with compassion rather than unnecessary force or actions that inflict suffering on animals."
She also urged the government, local authorities, relevant agencies, and the public to collaborate under the shared motto of "Compassion. Care. Community" to build a more humane society.
Key priorities, she said, included embedding animal welfare into public policy, instilling empathy in children from a young age through education, and translating compassion into concrete action via humane rescue, treatment and protection efforts.
"How society treats animals reflects its core character and failing to show empathy to the most vulnerable creatures will eventually erode compassion toward fellow human beings."
To ensure long-term deterrence, Her Royal Highness urged the government to review the penalties under the Animal Welfare Act 2015 to tighten punishments for animal abusers and ensure consistent nationwide enforcement.
"Compassion is not a sign of weakness. On the contrary, the ability to protect the most vulnerable creatures is the true measure of a society's strength, maturity, and civilisation."
Her Royal Highness' statement came in the wake of the public outcry following the killing of a pet dog during a capture operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang on July 29.
The dog catching operation was conducted by the Klang City Council following complaints from residents over safety concerns linked to an increase in stray dogs in the area.

Title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for 9 states, KL and Putrajaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nine states, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, are expected to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 7pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a weather warning issued at 3.45pm, said the affected areas in Perak are Manjung, Kinta, Perak Tengah, Kampar, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Batang Padang and Mualim.
On the east coast, the warning covers Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Kota Baru, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Bachok, Machang and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan, as well as Kuala Nerus, Hulu Terengganu, Kuala Terengganu, Marang, Dungun and Kemaman in Terengganu.
In Pahang, the affected areas are Raub, Bentong, Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, while in Negri Sembilan, the warning applies to Jelebu and Seremban.
MetMalaysia also issued the warning for the whole of Selangor, in addition to Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
In Johor, the affected areas are Tangkak, Segamat, Muar, Batu Pahat, Kluang, Mersing and Pontian.
For Sarawak, the warning covers Betong (Saratok and Kabong), Sarikei, Sibu (Kanowit), Mukah (Tanjung Manis and Daro), Kapit (Song), Miri (Beluru and Telang Usan), and Limbang.
In Sabah, the warning is in effect for the Interior Division (Tambunan), the West Coast and Kudat (Kota Marudu).

Title: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing attacks Asean peace plan, sets out priorities
Article:
NAYPYIDAW: Nearly four months after taking office, Myanmar's junta chief turned president Min Aung Hlaing on Friday criticised the regional Asean bloc's peace plan and outlined his government's plans for the war-torn Southeast Asian country.
Myanmar was plunged into turmoil in February 2021 when the military ousted an elected government led by Nobel Peace Prize winner Aung San Suu Kyi, sparking protests that expanded into a protracted civil war, killing some 100,000 people and displacing millions.
At the turn of this year, the military engineered a widely criticised election won by an army-backed party that allowed Min Aung Hlaing to transition into a civilian role. Following are some key points from his speech to parliament:
Dismissing Asean's peace plan – known as the "Five Point Consensus" – Min Aung Hlaing said the 11-member bloc has discriminated against Myanmar.
"We have been patient. We will respond to non-constructive actions on a case-by-case basis," he said, without referring to any specific member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.*His administration will hold by-elections in 2027 in 172 constituencies unable to vote during the December-January polls because of the ongoing unrest.
The government will enhance the capacity of the military and police, while continuing to implement a conscription law, he said.
His administration has invited rebel groups for talks without preconditions and, so far, has met with 13 ethnic armed organisations (EAOs).
The government is working to stop money laundering and arms smuggling by EAOs as well as cracking down on drug trafficking and online scam centres, Min Aung Hlaing said.
The government is prioritising the 1,400-km  India-Myanmar-Thailand trilateral highway project, as well as the 410-km Mandalay-Muse railway project to reach the border with China.* "The goal is to export goods to international markets in a short time at low cost," Min Aung Hlaing said.
The government is currently working on 10 power generation projects, including the controversial Myitsone dam, and efforts are also underway to build a nuclear power plant.
His government will allocate 10pct of the national budget for the education sector in the next fiscal year and up to 15pct in the 2028-2029 fiscal year.
The government is focusing on the tourism and agriculture sectors, and aims toboost domestic cotton production via loans and technical assistance for farmers, he said.
Large numbers of young people, aged between 18 and 34, have been leaving the country, impacting economic development, he said.
The military's conscription law is a major factor for this exodus, Reuters has previously reported.
"I will take two years to build momentum for constructing a new nation," he said. "I will also take three years to execute this build-up at full speed." --RUETERS

Title: DKU declares document dated April 19 unconstitutional
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has declared a document dated April 19 unconstitutional and in breach of Article X of the Negri Sembilan Constitution (UUTKNS) 1959.
Its secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, said the decision was made at a DKU meeting chaired by the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, yesterday.
He said the DKU meeting was attended by Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari; Undang of Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid; and Tunku Besar of Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, who fulfilled the requirements under Clause 20 of the UUTKNS 1959.
"The DKU has advised and ruled that Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad and Abdul Rahim Yasin have ceased to hold, or have never lawfully held, their respective positions.
"The Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong and Undang of Luak Jelebu were dismissed in accordance with the customary laws of their respective Luak on the applicable dates, while the purported Undang of Luak Rembau was never lawfully appointed under customary law as his appointment was not completed through the Istiadat Menzahirkan Kejadian Undang," he said in a statement here today.
Raja Norazli said the individuals had no legal authority to exercise the powers conferred under Article X of the UUTKNS 1959.
At the meeting, the DKU also considered and received a notification from the Ibu Soko and Anak-Anak Waris of Ayer, Luak Sungei Ujong, stating that holder of the hereditary Datuk Shahbandar Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid had been removed in accordance with the customary law of Luak Sungei Ujong, effective last Thursday.
He said that pursuant to Article XV (1) of the UUTKNS 1959, the position of Datuk Shahbandar of Sungei Ujong became automatically vacant.
"DKU takes note that the process of appointing the new Datuk Shahbandar of Sungei Ujong in accordance with the Luak Sungei Ujong customary law has yet to be concluded," he said.
The DKU is also looking into a complaint from Luak Jelebu concerning the unanimous decision by Waris, Anak Buah and Ibu Soko Waris Berundang Perut of Kemin Teriang, Kemin Beringin and Kemin Bemban to remove Maarof as the 16th Undang of Luak Jelebu, effective May 31, 2023, over the customary offences specified.
"Therefore, the position of Undang of Luak Jelebu is automatically vacant, and any action taken by Datuk Maarof after May 31, 2023, is deemed invalid.  Consequently, the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS) that he held while serving as Undang of Luak Jelebu is also forfeited," he said.
At the same meeting, the DKU also recognised that Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang of Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid were lawfully appointed according to the customary laws of their respective Luak.

Title: South Korea asked Prabowo to open dialogue with North Korea
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto said on Friday that South Korean President Lee Jae Myung asked him whether he could visit North Korea to open dialogue, adding that he would go.
Prabowo was speaking during a meeting with the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce.
As Prabowo spoke about Indonesia's pursuit of equally good relations with all countries, including China and The United States, he brought up the request made at his last visit to Seoul in April.
"During my last visit to South Korea, their president asked me if I could visit North Korea to open some kind of a dialogue. I told him, with all due respect and willingness, if you asked me to, I would go," he said.
"Indonesia is seen as having no interest in meddling in other countries' domestic affairs. We hold firm to that," he said.
In response, Lee's office said South Korea believed Indonesia and other countries with friendly ties to both Seoul and Pyongyang could play a constructive role in helping foster peaceful coexistence on the Korean peninsula, and that it had continued to explore ways to cooperate with them.
Indonesia traditionally has a non-aligned foreign policy.
It is not the first time Prabowo has expressed his willingness to mediate.
Indonesia's foreign minister Sugiono said in March that Prabowo was willing to ⁠be a mediator in the Iran war in a bid "to cool down and de-escalate the situation in the region."
Lee and Prabowo discussed energy security and agreed to expand cooperation in areas such as defence during the April meeting.
Lee has sought to ease tensions with Pyongyang since taking office last year, but repeated ⁠overtures ​for dialogue have been rebuffed ​by North Korea, which declared South Korea as a "hostile nation" in ​2024. --REUTERS

Title: Sultan of Pahang: Public roads are not racetracks
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, has urged the public to stop illegal street racing before more lives are lost, warning that such activities continue to endanger road users.
His Royal Highness reminded youths that their families were waiting for them to return home safely and that public roads should never be used to test courage or seek recognition.
"I am deeply saddened that some youths still choose public roads as a stage to seek fame, view the roar of engines as a symbol of bravery, and take pride in illegal street racing.
"More distressing is that this unhealthy culture is glorified on social media. Dangerous stunts are displayed for praise and attention, when the applause received today may end with parents' tears, lifelong regret and a lonely grave," he said.
Al-Sultan Abdullah said this during the investiture ceremony for state honours, awards and medals held in conjunction with His Royal Highness' 67th birthday celebration at Istana Abdulaziz today.
Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah.
On the issue of increasing foreigners' presence, including Rohingya refugees, he called on authorities to take firm action, including demolishing illegal structures built on government land if they were found to be unlawful settlements.
Al-Sultan Abdullah also urged the federal government to strengthen border controls, tighten entry procedures for foreigners, expedite the repatriation of illegal immigrants and take action against those involved.
"In my view, the most effective approach is to address the issue at the country's entry points, especially our waters, before they are able to establish a foothold and set up settlements.
"Preventing the problem at the border is far more effective than dealing with it after the situation has become complicated," he said.

Title: Search continues for Nirmal Purja-led team after Pakistan avalanche
Article:
SKARDU: Pakistan rescue teams resumed a high-altitude search on Saturday for seven climbers missing after a powerful avalanche on one of the world's highest peaks, with the remains of three mountaineers recovered.
The avalanche struck Thursday, cutting off contact with the ten-member international expedition led by renowned British-Nepali climber Nirmal Purja – who is not among the remains recovered so far.
Those recovered – flown by helicopter to hospital for formal identification – included an American woman, an Omani woman, and a Nepali man, the regional government said in a statement released Friday night.
Police in the mountainous northern Gilgit-Baltistan region said in a statement that high-altitude porters and rescue teams had begun a second day of the operation Saturday after the search was paused due to difficult weather conditions on Friday.
Rescuers and military helicopters had been scouring the area, and teams had stayed at the base camp overnight, according to the regional government.
"The rescue team has reported that they have spotted a few (more) dead bodies of the climbers through drone footage," the statement said.
"The rescue operation is being conducted under extremely challenging terrain and high-altitude weather conditions by the Pakistani army in coordination with local high-altitude climbers and rescuers," it added.
- POWERFUL AVALANCHE -
The avalanche struck while the mountaineers were on a mission to summit Broad Peak (8,047 metres, 26,400 feet) on Thursday while the team were ascending at an altitude of around 6,600 metres, according to regional authorities.
The expedition comprised 10 people – including Purja, five Nepalis, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American, and a climber from China.
The team were last in contact on Thursday morning, the official statement said, with reports emerging that evening of the powerful avalanche.
"Data from their tracking devices indicates that they were thrown hundreds of metres down the mountainside," Naila Kiani, from Pakistan's Alpine Club, told Le Monde newspaper.
- SUPER PEAKS -
Purja, 43, had written on X this week that he was close to becoming the first person to climb all 14 "super peaks" twice without oxygen.
"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down," he wrote.
Purja, who served with Britain's Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines, has broken multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide.
He climbed all 14 "eight-thousanders" (peaks above 8,000 metres) in six months and six days between April and October 2019 – then a record.
Broad Peak is the world's 12th highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range in northern Pakistan, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000-metre-plus ascents.
It was first summited in 1957 by an Austrian team.--AFP

Title: RCI report an opportunity to strengthen Tabung Haji, says minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) will not affect Malaysia's relationship with Saudi Arabia or its reputation for managing haj affairs.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the report should instead be viewed as an opportunity to further strengthen TH's management, governance and operations.
He said reforms implemented in recent years had brought about positive changes within the institution.
"We see this report as an opportunity to further strengthen and empower the overall management of Tabung Haji.
"Alhamdulillah, we have seen the recommendations being implemented, and today TH has undergone positive changes," he told reporters after attending the Program Madani Kita in Ampang today.
Zulkifli said TH's reserves had improved, dividend rates had increased and governance practices had been strengthened following the restructuring efforts.
He added that TH continued to receive international recognition for its haj management.
"There are several areas that we will continue to improve, including recommendations related to amendments to the Act.
"We have already held engagements with stakeholders and relevant parties, and InsyaAllah, we will gather the best feedback and input to further strengthen this institution."
Zulkifli was responding to questions on whether the findings and recommendations in the RCI report could affect Malaysia's image as a country recognised for its haj management system and its relationship with Saudi Arabia.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had earlier instructed that a special Dewan Rakyat sitting be held on Aug 11 to table and debate the findings of the RCI into TH, which examined the institution's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
The special sitting is expected to allow lawmakers to deliberate on the commission's findings and recommendations, including proposals to improve TH's governance, financial management and investment oversight.
The RCI found that TH faced financial weaknesses linked to high hibah payments, investment risks, accounting issues and governance shortcomings.
Among its findings, the commission said TH should have recorded a RM1.4 billion loss in 2017 instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported in its financial statements, after accounting for impairment losses and other adjustments.
The RCI also identified governance weaknesses, including broad ministerial powers over appointments, overlapping roles among directors and senior management, as well as concerns over political influence.
It recommended strengthening TH's governance framework through clearer criteria for board appointments, limiting active politicians from holding board positions, and improving oversight mechanisms.
The RCI also proposed separating the responsibilities of the minister responsible for religious affairs, who would oversee haj matters, from those of the finance minister, who would oversee financial management, funds and investments.
Other recommendations included conducting forensic audits of past investments, ensuring hibah payments are based on audited financial statements, strengthening audit oversight and improving the institution's professional management.
The RCI maintained that TH should remain a single institution, saying its weaknesses could be addressed through governance and operational reforms rather than major structural changes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Strong Malaysia-Bahrain ties underpin historic Bahrain GP at Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's selection to host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix following the disruption to the 2026 Formula 1 championship calendar marks a landmark arrangement underpinned by a shared commitment to motorsport excellence and the close ties between the two countries.
The race, scheduled for Oct 2 to 4 at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), will mark the first time the Bahrain Grand Prix has been staged outside the Kingdom since its inauguration in 2004, while retaining its official title.
The announcement was welcomed by F1 drivers and fans, with several teams also sharing messages and throwback posts from their previous races at SIC on social media following the confirmation.
Bahrain's Ambassador to Malaysia, Dr Waleed Khalifa Al Manea, said the arrangement reflected the strong ties between the royal and political leadership of both countries.
The arrangement reflects the strong ties between His Majesty King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, which were further strengthened during the Malaysian King's state visit to Bahrain in 2025. It also reflects the close communication and coordination between His Royal Highness Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, the Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Bahrain, and Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
"This high-level relationship and coordination helped facilitate the arrangements for hosting the event," he said in a written interview with Bernama.
Al Manea described the collaboration as unique and carries a broader significance for the bilateral relations.
"It reflects the high level of trust and cooperation between the two countries and represents another important step in strengthening bilateral relationship.
"It is unique because it brings together Bahrain's leadership and experience in motorsport with Malaysia's extensive experience and strong reputation in hosting Formula 1 and other world-class sporting events," he said.
The Ambassador said the race is expected to generate spillover benefits beyond motorsport, by creating opportunities for cooperation in tourism, aviation, transport, investment, hospitality and media.
"The race will be organised according to the highest international standards, while the launch of direct Gulf Air flights between Bahrain and Kuala Lumpur ahead of the event will further support travel and connectivity," he said.
The race will return Formula 1 to SIC for the first time since the Malaysian Grand Prix was last held there in 2017, when Red Bull Racing driver Max Verstappen claimed victory.
SIC hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix from 1999 to 2017, establishing itself as one of F1's best-known venues in Asia.
Though staged thousands of kilometres from Bahrain, the race will retain a subtle link to its traditional home, as both SIC and the Bahrain International Circuit were designed by renowned German circuit architect Hermann Tilke.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan of Pahang: No compromise on illegal land encroachment
Article:
KUANTAN: Every inch of the state's land must be protected from illegal encroachment and unlawful occupation, says the Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah.
His Royal Highness said the law must be enforced without fear or favour, and without compromise, whenever the sovereignty of Pahang's land and the dignity of the state were at stake.
"When the law is selectively enforced, justice begins to lose its meaning. And when justice collapses, the dignity of a state collapses with it," he said.
The ruler said this at the investiture ceremony for state honours, awards and medals held in conjunction with His Royal Highness' 67th birthday celebration at Istana Abdulaziz today.
Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah.
Al-Sultan Abdullah also urged the public not to be easily swayed by viral social media content or narratives designed to provoke sentiments.
He said some parties claimed to champion the people's interests but were instead worsening the situation by encouraging illegal land clearing and exploiting confusion.
"Some hide behind organisations, others shelter under political platforms, while some use their positions and influence to interfere in enforcement matters," he added.
Al-Sultan Abdullah said such actions did not represent a struggle for the people, but a betrayal of the state's interests and the rule of law.
"Anyone who incites people to break the law, protects encroachers, spreads misleading information or deliberately inflames the situation for personal interests must be investigated and appropriate action taken in accordance with the law," he said.
Meanwhile, he said more than 1.59 million hectares, or 44 per cent of Pahang's land area, remained gazetted as permanent forest reserves, with further areas set aside for conservation.
He said protecting forests involved significant costs, adding that Pahang had made a major contribution by preserving vast forest areas for the benefit of the nation and future generations.
"As such, these conservation efforts should continue to receive fairer support from the federal government through the ecological fiscal transfer mechanism, including appropriate financial allocations," he added.
The Sultan of Pahang also reminded members of the royal family and Orang Besar Pahang to uphold the good name of the Pahang royal institution.
At the ceremony, he announced the appointment of Pahang Investment, Industrial Development, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohammad Nizar Mohammad Najib as the new Orang Kaya Indera Shahbandar Pahang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Safar tour to allow contributors track wakaf progress firsthand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Wakaf contributors will no longer have to rely solely on reports or updates to track the impact of their contributions, as the Federal Territories Waqf Safar Tour Programme will allow them to visit completed projects firsthand.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the programme would be held regularly to strengthen confidence among existing contributors while encouraging more people to participate in wakaf.
"We are organising this programme to allow for wakaf contributors to visit the projects that have been implemented so they can see for themselves what has been carried out and the benefits provided.
"Insya-Allah, this programme will be held regularly and continuously to reassure existing contributors as well as potential contributors," he said at a press conference after launching the Federal Territories Waqf Safar Tour Programme Series 1 at the Darul Kifayah Complex in Batu Caves today.
Zulkifli said one of the key projects highlighted was the Federal Territory Islamic Religious Council (MAIWP) Islamic Education Excellence Complex in Putrajaya, which he described as a flagship initiative aimed at producing a generation of professionals equipped with both academic and religious knowledge.
He said the complex was developed by incorporating elements of heritage, technology, and both aqli (rational) and naqli (revealed) knowledge to meet the growing needs of the community.
Commenting on the first series of the Safar Tour Waqf Programme, Zulkifli said participants visited three waqf projects, with similar visits to be continued in future editions alongside improvements and the introduction of new projects.
"MAIWP and the zakat collection centre (PPZ) no longer want to only talk about concepts and theories.
"What we want to show is the implementation that has been translated into real projects, which are benefiting the community, the ummah and recipients," he said.
He explained that the programme was open to all available wakaf contributors, while those unable to attend could participate in future editions or follow project updates through their digital platforms.
"Those who have contributed their assets through waqf do not need to worry. They can rest assured because everything has been carried out and translated into actual implementation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Revive wakaf's golden era role beyond mosques and cemeteries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Wakaf institutions must be revived as a key driver of community development, as they were during the golden age of Islamic civilisation, rather than being viewed solely as sources of funding for mosques and burial grounds.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said wakaf could play a bigger role in advancing education, healthcare, research and economic development.
He said history showed that wakaf institutions were among the pillars of Islamic civilisation during its golden era in Baghdad, Andalusia and Istanbul.
"During that time, wakaf was not only for mosques or burial grounds, but also supported hospitals, universities, research and development (R&D)," he said when launching the Federal Territories Wakaf Safar Tour Programme Series 1 at the Darul Kifayah Complex in Batu Caves today.
Zulkifli said strengthening the wakaf sector could reduce society's reliance on the government while fostering a more independent and empowered community.
He said the Safar Tour Wakaf Programme aimed to promote wakaf as both an act of worship and a catalyst for ummah economic development through visits to projects that directly benefit the community.
"When people understand and see the impact of wakaf themselves, they will become more confident and encouraged to contribute, while helping to build a culture of wakaf," he said.
Meanwhile, Zulkifli suggested that the Federal Territories Islamic Religious Council (MAIWP) and MAIWP Zakat Collection Centre (PPZ-MAIWP) introduce virtual reality (VR) experiences to allow contributors to see projects developed through their wakaf contributions.
He said MAIWP's zakat collection had exceeded RM1.2 billion and was expected to reach about RM1.3 billion this year, but the wakaf sector had yet to achieve similar progress.
"We want to spark a new revival so society develops a culture of wakaf.
"Everyone can contribute to wakaf, and it is among the deeds that bring great rewards in the hereafter," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chief Justice heads Pahang honours list
Article:
KUANTAN: Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh heads the list of 52 recipients of Pahang state honours, awards and medals, in an investiture ceremony held in conjunction with the 67th birthday celebration of Sultan Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah.
Al-Sultan Abdullah presented the awards at Balai Mahkota, Istana Abdulaziz here today.
Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah.
Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and state government leaders were also in attendance.
Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Sri Setia Al-Sultan Abdullah Ahmad Shah Pahang (SAAS) award, which carries the title of Datuk Seri Setia.
The Sri Sultan Ahmad Shah Pahang (SSAP) award, which carries the title of Datuk Seri, was conferred on 16 people, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi and Dewan Rakyat deputy speaker Datuk Dr Ramli Mohd Nor, who is also the Cameron Highlands MP.
Also receiving the SSAP award were Deputy Minister of Economy and Paya Besar MP Datuk Mohd Shahar Abdullah and Pahang Local Government, Housing, Environment and Green Technology Committee chairman Datuk Mohammad Fakhruddin Mohd Ariff.
Other recipients included Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman, Customs Department director-general Datuk Amran Ahmad, Local Government Department director-general Datuk Mohd Fadzli Mohd Kenali and International Islamic University Malaysia rector Professor Emeritus Datuk Dr Osman Bakar.
Joining the list of SSAP recipients were Universiti Tun Abdul Razak (UniRazak) chancellor Datuk Mohamed Nizam Abdul Razak, Armed Forces Joint Forces commander Lieutenant-General Datuk Tengku Muhammad Fauzi Tengku Ibrahim and Deputy Air Force Chief Lieutenant General Datuk Nur Hafis Abdul Karim.
Also receiving the honour were Air Education and Training commander Lieutenant General Datuk Muhammad Tarminzi Mustapha and singer Datuk Shaheila Abdul Majid, better known as Sheila Majid.
The Sultan of Pahang also conferred the Sri Indera Mahkota Pahang (SIMP) award, which carries the title of Datuk Indera, on two recipients, namely Koperasi Serbausha Makmur Berhad (Kosma) chairman Datuk Zamri Mohamed and Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (MATRADE) chief executive officer Datuk Abu Bakar Yusof.
Eight people were conferred the Darjah Sultan Ahmad Shah Pahang (DSAP) award, which carries the title of Datuk, including Pahang Syariah Chief Judge Datuk Abdul Walid Abu Hassan, Naval Area 1 commander Rear Admiral Azman Rabani and Faiza Sdn Bhd managing director Faiza Bawumi Sayed Ahmad.
Pahang Communications and Multimedia, Youth, Sports and Non-Governmental Organisation Committee chairman Fadzli Mohamad Kamal was among 18 recipients conferred the Darjah Indera Mahkota Pahang (DIMP) award, which carries the title of Datuk.
Other recipients of the DIMP award included Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department Deputy Director-General (Operations) Nordin Pauzi, Pahang Education director Ahmad Zamri Md Isa and Tenaga Nasional Berhad Pahang general manager Affendi Abdul Rahman.
Also receiving the DIMP award were MFDM Holdings Sdn Bhd director Mohd Qabil Ambak Mahamad Fathil, who is also an equestrian athlete, and national silat exponent Mohd Al-Jufferi Jamari.
During the ceremony, the Sultan of Pahang also conferred the Setia Ahmad Shah Pahang (SAP) award on two recipients, the Setia Mahkota Pahang (SMP) award on one recipient, and the Ahli Ahmad Shah Pahang (AAP) and Ahli Mahkota Pahang (AMP) awards on two recipients each. – BERNAMA

Title: Perkep taps KJH to expand market for its products
Article:
KOTA SAMARAHAN: Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) Sarawak Segulai Sejalai has provided an ideal platform for the Police Family Association (Perkep) to expand the market reach of products produced by its entrepreneurs.
Perkep chairman Puan Sri Munirah Che Rose said the association's maiden participation in the carnival enabled it to introduce a range of handmade products produced by wives of police officers and personnel.
She said the participation was not only aimed at promoting locally made products but also at raising public awareness of Perkep's role in empowering the economic wellbeing of police families.
"KJH provides us with a valuable opportunity to introduce handmade products created by Perkep members, who are wives of police officers and personnel.
"It is the best platform to showcase their hard work and creativity to the public," she said when met at the Perkep booth at the carnival.
Munirah said Perkep had also been invited to participate in the KJH series across the country.
She said the initiative would help expand the market reach of products made by Perkep entrepreneurs while creating more business networking opportunities.
She added that continued participation in programmes such as KJH would enhance the commercial value of members' products and strengthen Perkep's image as an association committed to empowering entrepreneurs among police families.
Perkep's debut at the Kota Samarahan edition of the carnival is also expected to pave the way for closer collaboration with the organisers, ensuring greater exposure for its members' products at future KJH events nationwide.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No repeat of Dataran Merdeka mess, says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Members of the public attending the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 have been urged to act responsibly by disposing of their rubbish at designated areas to ensure the venue remains clean.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she did not want a repeat of the recent incident at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur, where large amounts of rubbish were left behind following a public gathering.
"Maintaining cleanliness is a shared responsibility. It is not solely the responsibility of Putrajaya Corporation (PPj) to collect rubbish after an event.
"Imagine coming to celebrate National Day, only to leave behind an area covered with rubbish. I do not think that creates a good impression, and I urge everyone present to dispose of their waste in the bins provided," she told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita (PMK) programme with the Putrajaya Federal Territory community today.
The event was also attended by PPj president Datuk Mohd Sakeri Abdul Kadir.
During the programme, Hannah presented mock cheques representing a special contribution of RM5,000 from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to selected Kawasan Rukun Tetangga or Neighbourhood Watch areas.
Hannah said her office was currently focusing on efforts to raise public awareness and believes the public has learned from the recent rubbish accumulation incident at Dataran Merdeka.
She added that PPj would increase the number of rubbish bins at strategic locations and enhance waste collection frequency to ensure the celebration area remains clean and comfortable.
"I will also ensure that PPj issues reminders and announcements to everyone present to dispose of their rubbish properly. This is a shared responsibility and not just the duty of local authorities to clean up after an event," she said.
On July 20, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) conducted cleanup operations at
Dataran Merdeka
after the area was left littered following a large gathering to watch the live broadcast of the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
DBKL said waste collection would continue, but added that maintaining the cleanliness of the capital should not depend solely on the efforts of cleaning workers after the public has left.
The 2026 National Day celebration would be held at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 on a moderate yet vibrant scale.
"Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati" has been selected as the theme for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM2026) celebrations, while the Malaysia Madani logo will continue to be used as the official logo for the celebrations until next year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Homecoming rush: Voters return, traffic builds across Negri Sembilan
Article:
SEREMBAN: Traffic flow on several major routes around Seremban, as well as connecting roads to outlying districts such as Bukit Putus, Kuala Pilah and Kuala Klawang in Jelebu, has been reported to be steadily building since early this morning.
The surge is attributed to outstation voters returning to their hometowns to cast their ballots in the 16th Negri Sembilan election.
Real-time traffic checks on Google Maps, Waze and Apple Maps revealed slow-moving traffic at several hotspots, particularly along the Seremban-Kuala Pilah road through Bukit Putus, the Seremban-Tampin route, and roads leading to Kuala Klawang in Jelebu.
Rain in several areas of the district around midday further compounded the situation.
In Seremban city centre, a Bernama survey observed a marked increase in vehicles on several main roads, with motorists believed to be making their way to polling centres, most of which are situated close to major thoroughfares.
Over in villages, the typically quiet weekend atmosphere has also transformed, with rows of vehicles lining narrow roads, while eateries and breakfast stalls have been enjoying increased patronage from larger crowds than usual.
Meanwhile, Negri Sembilan Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Supt Roslan Mohamed@Ab Aziz, when contacted, said conditions remained under control as of 2pm despite the noticeable increase in vehicles.
"There have been some delays at toll plazas due to the higher volume of vehicles entering Negri Sembilan, but traffic personnel have been deployed at key locations to help ease the flow and manage the situation," he said.
He added that police expected the number of vehicles to continue rising towards the evening peak period, but monitoring and on-ground deployment of personnel would be maintained to ensure traffic flow remains manageable.
Today, 859,760 voters across Negri Sembilan are fulfilling their duty to elect new representatives for 36 state assembly seats, ultimately determining the state government for the next term.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tun Jugah-inspired hairstyle draws crowds at KJH Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak Tourism Board (STB) marketing administrative officer Ozie Tunggeng has been turning heads at the Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) Sarawak Segulai Sejalai with a distinctive hairstyle inspired by the legendary Iban leader, Tun Jugah anak Barieng.
Ozie said his unique appearance has attracted the curiosity of visitors, particularly those from Peninsular Malaysia, who are keen to learn more about his background and heritage.
"Many visitors come up to ask where I am from and what my ethnicity is because they are intrigued by my appearance," he said when met at the STB booth during the carnival.
"I am a Bidayuh from Bau, but my grandmother is Iban, and I can speak several Sarawakian dialects."
Ozie said he adopted the iconic look to reflect his role as a cultural activist while promoting Sarawak as a tourism destination.
Throughout the carnival, Ozie has been promoting the state's tourism products and hosting interactive stage activities, including tourism quizzes.
Now participating in KJH for the third time, he said the carnival continues to attract overwhelming public interest, making it an ideal platform to engage directly with visitors.
STB assistant marketing officer Nabil Aiman Sait said the board remains committed to promoting Sarawak's tourism offerings to both domestic and international visitors.
He said one of its key priorities is raising awareness of lesser-known attractions, including the state's national parks and nature reserves.
"Many locals are still unaware of the full range of Sarawak's tourism offerings, including admission fees for certain destinations.
"KJH provides us with an excellent platform to share accurate and up-to-date information with visitors," he said.
Nabil said STB's third consecutive participation in the carnival had delivered encouraging results by increasing public awareness of the state's tourism assets.
He also encouraged Sarawakians to explore their home state before travelling abroad.
Echoing similar sentiments, SarawakTourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Ministry assistant administrative officer Norasma Faiznur Bujang said they had brought together all agencies under its purview to showcase a wide range of initiatives throughout the carnival.
Besides promoting tourism and the creative industry, she said the ministry is also raising public awareness of the upcoming 2027 SEA Games in Sarawak as part of efforts to strengthen the state's position as a leading regional destination for major international events.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mental health stigma leaves many suffering in silence, says Queen
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has expressed concern that the stigma surrounding mental health continues to prevent many people from seeking professional help, leaving them to suffer in silence.
Citing New Straits Times reports on the growing mental health crisis, Her Majesty said adults were increasingly burdened by financial hardship, debt and strained family relationships, often leading to severe psychological distress.
"Studies carried out by NST also show that 16.5 per cent of children aged five to 15 struggle with mental health problems.
"And one in four adolescents aged 13 to 17 experiences depression," Her Majesty said at the University of Reading Malaysia's 10th convocation ceremony today.
Raja Zarith Sofiah, who received an Honorary Doctorate in Psychology from the university, said addressing the nation's mental health challenges had never been more important.
She said understanding human behaviour, resilience and relationships was fundamental to building stronger communities and a more harmonious society.
Her Majesty also lamented the rise of hate speech and growing intolerance despite unprecedented access to information.
"It is a sad irony that, at a time when knowledge is more accessible than ever through websites, social media and podcasts, we have become less tolerant, less kind, and continue to focus on our differences rather than our shared humanity," she said.
Raja Zarith Sofiah said universities must do more than equip graduates with technical knowledge, stressing the need to nurture character, sound judgement and strong moral values.
Quoting the late Royal Professor Tan Sri Dr Syed Muhammad Naquib Al-Attas, she said the true purpose of education was to cultivate virtuous individuals, not merely skilled workers.
Citing the teachings of Imam al-Ghazali that knowledge without action is of little value, the Queen urged graduates to use what they had learned for the greater good.
Her Majesty also thanked the university for the honorary doctorate and congratulated the graduates, reminding them that their success would ultimately be measured by the positive impact they make on society.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nerves, pride as 1st time voters cast their ballots
Article:
SEREMBAN: For many first-time voters in the 16th Negri Sembilan election today, casting their ballot was a memorable milestone marked by excitement, nerves and pride.
Fashion designer Hani Eriqa Mazlan, 21, said voting for the first time gave her a deeper appreciation of the democratic process.
"I was nervous and my hands were shaking because it was my first time voting. I had always known about elections, but going through the process myself felt completely different.
"I have followed the issues and know what is best for Negri Sembilan. Today, we make our choice," she said after voting at Sekolah Menengah Agama Dato' Klana Petra Maamor.
Hani Eriqa arrived with her younger sister, Hani Mazri Eyna, 20, who was also voting for the first time, along with five other family members.
The college student said the experience reinforced the importance of every vote in choosing representatives who would champion the people's interests.
"I was a little nervous but also excited because it was my first opportunity to fulfil my responsibility as a voter," she said.
Meanwhile, college student M. Lavinesh Nair, 18, said he initially felt overwhelmed by the large crowd when he arrived at the polling centre with his family.
"I was nervous because there were so many people and I was a little confused at first. But the Election Commission officers were very helpful and guided me through the process.
"Now that I have voted, I know what the experience is really like," he said.
As of 11am, voter turnout stood at 28.11 per cent.
A total of 859,760 registered voters, including 7,391 postal voters, are eligible to vote today to elect representatives for the state's 36 legislative assembly seats, with 103 candidates contesting.
Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, with 14,995 voters casting their ballots, surpassing the Election Commission's 90 per cent target.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CAP calls for tougher screening for pilots after Jakarta drug case
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) has called for tougher screening and continuous monitoring of pilots following the arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Jakarta over alleged drug smuggling.
CAP president Mohideen Abdul Kader said the association was "shocked and disappointed" by the incident, calling it a major blow to Malaysia's aviation industry and public confidence in air travel.
He said passenger safety must remain the highest priority, as travellers entrust their lives to pilots every time they board an aircraft.
"Passengers expect pilots to be responsible for their lives on a flight. They have the right to expect pilots to be physically and mentally fit because they pay for their flight tickets.
"We urge airlines to strengthen their recruitment processes by ensuring pilots are free from tobacco, alcohol and drugs, while introducing stricter health monitoring throughout their careers," he said today.
It was reported yesterday that a Malaysian pilot was arrested for allegedly attempting to smuggle a large quantity of drugs, including more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg, into Indonesia recently.
In reports published by Kompas.com and Suara.com, Indonesian authorities also found 2.74g of methamphetamine, as well as 0.0825g of methamphetamine residue in a glass pipe, when the suspect was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport about 11.30pm local time on Tuesday.
Mohideen said all pilots and co-pilots should undergo thorough medical examinations and fitness assessments before operating flights to ensure they are
fit to fly
.
"The bigger issue is whether the alleged drug use could have been detected earlier through mandatory medical examinations and fitness assessments. This is an area that requires stricter monitoring," he added.
Mohideen also called on cabin crew members to report to the relevant authorities any suspicious behaviour or signs that a pilot might be unfit for duty.
"We are talking about the lives of hundreds of passengers, including children. Even if such incidents are rare, precautions are essential because there is no room for complacency when it comes to aviation safety," he said.
He stressed that the actions of a small number of undisciplined pilots should not tarnish the reputation of the many professionals in the industry.
Mohideen described the incident as a "major embarrassment" for Malaysia's aviation sector and said stronger preventive measures were needed to maintain public confidence and ensure the highest standards of flight safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
